clue.text: Tom honoured in song

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British honour

explanation.surface: A man named Tom is celebrated in a ballad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' looks like a man's name but is a tomcat; 'honoured' is the CH a Companion of Honour puts after their name.
explanation.definitionFit: A catch is a type of round sung by several voices, so it is a kind of song.

clue.text: Blimey! Scotsman overcomes the German seed!

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece overcoming another sits above it

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like blimey
Ian is a typical Scottish name
der is German for the

explanation.surface: Astonished, a Scot gets the better of a German in a seed contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Coriander seed is a spice from the plant of the same name.

clue.text: Tadpole's companion, Dizzy type. light-headed

definitions.meaning: in Disraeli's novel Coningsby, Tadpole and his partner are political hacks; Dizzy was Disraeli's nickname
a thin candle that is lit at its top

explanation.definitionFit: Taper is Tadpole's crony in Disraeli's Coningsby, and a thin candle burns with a flame on its head.

clue.text: Trite sayings, but they have cutting effect

parts.note: hack means hackneyed, trite
saws are old sayings or proverbs

explanation.surface: Worn-out proverbs can still be cutting.
explanation.definitionFit: Hacksaws are fine-toothed saws for cutting metal.

clue.text: Appeasement? History has no love for false reasoning

parts.note: a sop is something offered to placate or appease

indicators.note: the word History is said to lack something, so a letter comes out of it

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A historian sneers that appeasing the enemy was bad logic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no love' takes the O out of HISTORY, leaving HISTRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophistry is clever but specious argument meant to deceive.

clue.text: Plague, problem with lame dogs caught by coppers

indicators.note: one piece is held inside another, as if caught

parts.note: coppers are copper coins, pennies, so pence
from the saying about helping a lame dog over a stile

explanation.surface: Police officers deal with a nuisance involving injured dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'help a lame dog over a stile' makes the stile the lame dog's obstacle.
explanation.definitionFit: Pestilence is a deadly epidemic disease, a plague.

clue.text: Doctor isn't worried about this description of heart

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the doctor
worried letters are disturbed and rearranged

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor claims to be unconcerned about a patient's heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is the medical officer, not a verb; 'worried' is the anagram signal on isn't, and 'about' makes the shuffled letters surround the doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: One's innermost heart is the deepest, most private part of it.

clue.text: Self-restrained method of painting, note

parts.note: tempera is painting with pigment bound in egg
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A calm style of painting, noted.
explanation.definitionFit: Being temperate means showing moderation and self-control.

clue.text: They dismiss the German eight from this boat

definitions.text: They dismiss the German eight from this boat

parts.words: They dismiss the German eight from this boat
parts.note: take the German word for eight out of the vessel's name and only the letter Y remains, which sounds like a short form of they

explanation.definitionFit: A yacht is a sailing or pleasure vessel.

clue.text: USA air-cop is out for grabs

indicators.note: being out means being disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An American air policeman is ready to seize whatever he can.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR gave 'air-top'; the page prints 'air-cop'. Rearrange USAAIRCOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Being out for grabs describes a greedy, grasping nature, which is what rapacious means.

clue.text: Ape about to pursue Bohemian girl

indicators.note: one piece pursuing another comes after it in the answer

parts.note: Mimi is the heroine of Puccini's opera La Boheme
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A monkey runs about chasing a girl from Bohemia.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to copy or imitate them.

clue.text: Check the second half-year balance

indicators.note: the second half of the following word is kept, its last two letters

parts.note: the balance is the rest or remainder

explanation.surface: A firm checks its accounts for the closing six months.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrest something is to halt or check its progress.

clue.text: Bad sort of youth, getting a maiden into prison

parts.note: a miss is an unmarried girl or maiden
pent means shut in or confined, as if put into prison

explanation.surface: A wayward young man ends up getting a girl locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'a misspent youth' makes the definition fair: it describes a youth wasted.
explanation.definitionFit: A wasted, idle youth is called misspent, a stock phrase.

clue.text: Up, Robin! (see 17)

parts.note: being up on a horse means riding
Robin Hood is the outlaw of Sherwood

explanation.surface: Up on horseback, Robin calls out.
explanation.walkthrough: With 17 down it completes the fairy tale Little Red Riding Hood.
explanation.definitionFit: Together with the answer to 17 down it names the girl in the wolf story.

clue.text: Bearer of dishes, also in the silent service?

definitions.meaning: a small lift carrying food between kitchen and dining room
read literally, a mute servant at table

explanation.definitionFit: A dumb-waiter is a food lift, and a waiter who cannot speak would serve in silence.

clue.text: Many cavorting in lagoon of Kubla Khan

parts.note: M is a thousand in Roman numerals, a large number

indicators.note: cavorting means prancing about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Lots of people frolic in the lake by Kubla Khan's palace.
explanation.walkthrough: Kubla Khan was a grandson of Genghis Khan, ruling the Mongol empire.
explanation.definitionFit: Kublai Khan was a Mongol emperor, so things belonging to him are of that nation.

clue.text: Post of bodyguard

definitions.meaning: letters sent through the postal system

explanation.definitionFit: Mail is both letters delivered and the linked metal armour protecting a knight's body.

clue.text: Minor revolutionary takes 13 to a pantomime

parts.note: minor means small or little
a red is a revolutionary communist

explanation.surface: A young radical takes someone to the Christmas show.
explanation.walkthrough: With 13 down it completes the fairy tale that is a pantomime favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Joined to the answer of 13 down it names the heroine of a pantomime story.

clue.text: Direct return of brief in this month

indicators.note: the turned word sits inside the abbreviation

parts.note: inst. is short for instant, meaning this month in old letters

indicators.note: return means the word for brief is read backwards

parts.note: curt means brief or short

explanation.surface: Instructions for sending back a summary this month.
explanation.walkthrough: Inst., short for instant, was old business-letter usage for this month. 'return of' turns the word for brief backwards before 'in' places it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To instruct is to give orders, to direct someone.

clue.text: Private row

definitions.meaning: an example of a military grade
a line of soldiers side by side

explanation.definitionFit: A private is the lowest military grade, and a line of soldiers abreast is also so called.

clue.text: Unhappiness with record on portable accommodation

parts.note: a gramophone record is a disc
a tent is shelter you can carry

explanation.surface: Camping misery: the record player perched on the tent.
explanation.definitionFit: Discontent is dissatisfaction, a lack of contentment.

clue.text: The rest of Spain

parts.note: not the remainder of the country, but the Spanish afternoon nap

explanation.definitionFit: A siesta is an afternoon sleep, a custom in Spain.

clue.text: Low circles — some connexions with shipping

parts.note: to low is to moo like a cow
rings are circles

explanation.surface: Lowly circles have their links with the shipping trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' is the cow's sound, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Moorings are the ropes, chains and anchors that tie a vessel to its berth.

clue.text: Theme's proper order reversed

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: reversed means the joined words are read backwards

parts.note: fit means proper or suitable
OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: A theme is just the right order turned back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A motif is a recurring theme in music or art.

clue.text: Proceed in an easy way, with nautical gait

definitions.text: Proceed in an easy way, with nautical gait

parts.words: Proceed in an easy way, with nautical gait
parts.note: a leisurely walk, described with a hint at the rolling walk of a sailor

explanation.definitionFit: To stroll is to walk at an easy, unhurried pace.

clue.text: Gloomy, having no opener for the game

indicators.note: lacking an opener means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: sombre means gloomy

explanation.surface: Downcast at losing the first player for the match.
explanation.definitionFit: Ombre is an old card game for three players, popular in the 17th and 18th centuries.

clue.text: Set her in The Wanderer's Return

indicators.note: return means the run of letters is read backwards
in says the letters lie inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: A woman appears in a story about a traveller coming home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' takes ANDE from inside Wanderer's, and 'Return' turns it back.
explanation.definitionFit: Edna is a woman's name, so it can stand for a woman, her.

clue.text: Bull's after the two of them? On the contrary

definitions.text: Bull's after the two of them? On the contrary

parts.words: Bull's after the two of them? On the contrary
parts.note: in the zodiac the sign of the bull, Taurus, comes before Gemini, so the pair follow the bull

explanation.walkthrough: Gemini, the third sign, is symbolised by a pair of brothers; it follows Taurus the bull.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini is the sign of the heavenly brothers born together, Castor and Pollux.

clue.text: One such queer lot precedes this clue

parts.note: odd means strange or queer
a number is a group or lot

explanation.surface: A strange group of people goes ahead of this crossword hint.
explanation.walkthrough: This clue is numbered 27, which is one such: the definition points at the figure printed before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty-seven cannot be divided by two, so it belongs to that class of integers.

clue.text: Symphonic poem and one in final form

indicators.note: the letter for one goes inside the rearranged words
the words are put into a new form, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A tone poem and one movement in its finished shape.
explanation.walkthrough: Sibelius's piece is named for his homeland. 'form' rearranges the two words, and 'in' places the one inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Sibelius wrote Finlandia, a patriotic tone poem for orchestra.
